Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
Our community organizer rallied the neighborhood against a highway expansion she claimed would destroy local parks. She led protests, collected signatures, and ultimately 'saved' us. A leaked internal memo later revealed she'd fabricated the proposed route entirely—the transportation department had never planned any construction near our area. She manufactured a threat to become the hero who defeated it.

CANDIDATE A:
Our community organizer rallied the neighborhood against a proposed highway expansion. An independent environmental review confirmed the project would damage local ecosystems as she'd claimed. Her opposition addressed a documented threat, and the successful campaign protected measurable community interests.

CANDIDATE B:
The lifeguard at our pool kept 'rescuing' struggling swimmers in the deep end. Parents praised his vigilance and quick reactions. A maintenance worker noticed he'd been adjusting the pool's filtration to create disorienting currents near the diving area. He was creating the emergencies he heroically resolved.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:31"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve someone fabricating a threat or danger to appear as a hero by resolving the situation they created."}
